    {

        if ($utf8Formula !== $functionString) {

        $inPath = false;
        $inRange = false;

        $rangeCount = 0;
        $errorCount = 0;

                    if ($nextChar === FormulaParser::QUOTE_DOUBLE) {
                        $buffer .= $nextChar;
                        ++$index;
                    } else {
                        $inString = false;
                    }
                }
                ++$index;

                continue;
            }

            if ($inPath) {
                $buffer .= $char;
                if ($char === FormulaParser::QUOTE_SINGLE) {
                    if ($nextChar === FormulaParser::QUOTE_SINGLE) {
                        $buffer .= $nextChar;
                        ++$index;
                    } else {
                        $inPath = false;
                    }
                }
                ++$index;

                continue;
            }

            if ($inRange) {
                $buffer .= $char;
                $inRange = ($char !== FormulaParser::BRACKET_CLOSE);
                ++$index;

                continue;
            }

            if ($inError) {
                $errorLiteral .= $char;
                $buffer .= $char;
                ++$index;
                if (Functions::isError($errorLiteral) === true) {
                    ++$errorCount;
                    $inError = false;
                    $errorLiteral = '';
                } elseif (strlen($errorLiteral) >= 14) {

                    $errorLiteral = '';

part.text:
Fixed. The `XLFNREGEXP` regex in `src/PhpSpreadsheet/Writer/Xlsx/FunctionPrefix.php:12` had no word-boundary assertion, so the `days` alternative matched the tail of `NETWORKDAYS`, producing `NETWORK_xlfn.DAYS`. Adding `\b` before the function-name alternation ensures `_xlfn.` is only prefixed to standalone `days` (and other `_xlfn` functions), leaving `NETWORKDAYS` untouched.

Validation:
- `FunctionPrefixTest`: 13/13 pass (includes the new `DAYS`/`NETWORKDAYS` cases that previously failed).
- Writer tests: only 5 pre-existing `DrawingsTest` errors remain (identical on baseline).
- Calculation/Functions tests: 5 pre-existing `RowOnSpreadsheetTest` failures remain (identical on baseline); no new failures.
